results.attack: mutate each receipt field in turn and re-verify
results.note: the receipt self-verifies and all 15 single-field mutations, including a substituted contentDigest, fail verification

results.attack: one record copied to fifty, then permuted
results.note: records 1 -> 50, distinctRoots stays 1, margin stays 1, conclusion stays absent_within_declared_scope; the permuted flood has an identical contentDigest

results.attack: receipt asserts a location was unavailable while carrying evidence that could only have come from it
results.note: CONFIRMED UNDETECTABLE, as preregistered. Schema v0.1 has no record-to-location link, so the contradiction is invisible. The coverage gate still refuses absence, which bounds the damage but does not detect the lie. Reported whatever the result, per PROTOCOL.md.

results.attack: presence claim at a tie, at a strict minority, and at a strict majority
results.note: tie -> not_established, minority -> not_established, majority -> supported. This is the owner decision that reversed this implementation's v1.0.0 reading; it is pinned here so a later regression is caught. Note R1 also makes `present` and `absent_within_declared_scope` unreachable for presence claims, which this implementation already satisfied.

results.attack: receipt whose proposition carries a quote, a backslash, an em dash and an accented letter
results.note: escaping follows canonicalForm.stringEscaping: '\"' and '\\' escaped, U+2014 and U+00E9 emitted as raw UTF-8 with no \uXXXX form, and the receipt self-verifies. This tests the codec against the stated rule; it does NOT test it against the reference, which only C11 can do.

baselines.note: Run against the full 176,120-world exhaustive set, not a subsample. Halting is disabled for baselines so that complete counts are obtained. B2p is not preregistered; it is B2 with an honest search block, and it exists to isolate the I2a/I2b split. FINDING: B2p is byte-identical to B3 on every world. The preregistration's B2 ('counts distinct roots but ignores the search ledger') and B3 ('full root collapse, no coverage requirement for absence') describe the SAME ablation unless B2 is additionally taken to fabricate its search block, which is the reading used for the registered B2 here.

c11DigestAnalysis.diagnosis: See finding G2. R4 defines the canonical FORM (codec) and the digest SCOPE (which member is removed) but does not define the receipt OBJECT. canonicalForm.digestScope enumerates covered members including `schema`, `reason` and `limits`; the value of none of these is stated anywhere in the v1.1.0 package, nor is the receipt's member list registered. A conforming codec therefore still cannot reproduce this digest, because the bytes it must hash are not specified. The byte-length gap below quantifies exactly how much of the hashed content is unregistered.

digestByteBudget.membersCounted: transactionId, claim{type,proposition}, search{4}, evidence{7}, conclusion -- all taken from C11's own input and expected blocks
digestByteBudget.note: 40% of the bytes C11 pins are the values of three members that R4 names as covered by the digest and that no document in the package defines. No conforming implementation can compute this digest from the specification alone.

canonicalFormConformance.externalCrossCheck: The unsigned canonical form this implementation produces for C11 was independently round-tripped through the protocol's own stated realisation, python json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8'), and is BYTE-IDENTICAL to it. The codec therefore conforms to canonicalForm; the C11 digest mismatch is not a codec defect. See c11DigestAnalysis and finding G2.

repairR1Surface.note: Both distributions computed in this run over the same 176,120 worlds. The IND-20260807-1 column is what this implementation reported under v1.0.0; reproducing it here confirms the only thing that changed is the reading, not the enumeration.
repairR1Surface.repair: R1 (owner decision): presence concludes `supported` iff distinct supporting roots strictly exceed distinct opposing roots; ties are not_established.

repairR1TestSurface.ablation: B5 with R1 inverted -- i.e. exactly the IND-20260807-1 reading, in which a tie or a strict minority still concludes `supported`.
repairR1TestSurface.finding: See G4. If invariantViolationsDetected is 0, then no invariant in the registered set constrains the presence conclusion, and the entire enforcement of R1 -- a rule the protocol measures at 22,440 exhaustive worlds -- rests on the fixtures listed above. v1.1.0 repaired the specification text that allowed the divergence; it did not add a checker that would detect the divergence recurring. This is the same structural defect PROTOCOL.md v1.1.0 diagnoses in its own words ('No invariant constrains conclusion, so the divergence was invisible to the entire v1.0.0 test surface') -- still true of the v1.1.0 test surface.
repairR1TestSurface.question: Do the eleven v1.1.0 invariants have power against a wrong presence rule?
